cases.title: Crystal weapon seed
cases.semanticExcerpt:
[[File:Crystal weapon seed detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''crystal weapon seed''' is an [[elves|elven]] [[crystal]] that can be turned into [[crystal weapons]]. Completing the [[Gauntlet]] will yield a chance of gaining these seeds. The crystal weapon seed can be bought from [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]] for 12 [[Last Man Standing]] points.
cases.positiveFunctionExcerpt: This seed can be restored into a [[crystal bow]], a [[crystal shield]], or a [[crystal halberd]], the latter only with completion of the [[Hard Western Provinces Diary]]. Before completion of [[Song of the Elves]], [[Ilfeen]] is the only one to offer this service to the player. She can be found at either of two clearings in [[Isafdar]], teleporting between them periodically. If the player is mid-quest, and she is occupied with the fight against [[Lord Iorwerth]], an [[Elven Scout]] will fulfil her role. After completion of the quest, [[Ilfeen]] is found in [[Prifddinas]], slightly south of the house portal.

[[File:Crystal weapon seed detail.png|left|130px]]
A '''crystal weapon seed''' is an [[elves|elven]] [[crystal]] that can be turned into [[crystal weapons]]. Completing the [[Gauntlet]] will yield a chance of gaining these seeds. The crystal weapon seed can be bought from [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]] for 12 [[Last Man Standing]] points.

==Enchantment costs==
===Ilfeen===
{{#vardefine:crystalshardvalue|{{#ifexpr:{{#vardefineecho:seedvalue|{{GEP|Enhanced crystal teleport seed}} / 150}} > {{#vardefineecho:divinesupercombatvalue|({{GEP|Divine super combat potion(4)}} - {{GEP|Super combat potion(4)}}) / 0.4}} | {{#var:seedvalue}} | {{#var:divinesupercombatvalue}}}}}}
If the player has a crystal weapon seed, [[Ilfeen]] can enchant it into a [[crystal bow]], [[crystal shield|shield]], or [[crystal halberd|halberd]] for coins. Having her sing halberds requires completion of the [[Hard Western Provinces Diary]]. Ilfeen '''cannot''' "recharge" the crystal items themselves, players must manually revert their item to a crystal weapon seed and choose the item that they want to pay her for. While singing yourself with [[Crystal shard|shards]] always costs {{NoCoins|({{#var:crystalshardvalue}} * 40) round 0|c}}, the price she charges depends on how many times she has previously been paid to enchant weapon seeds, down to a minimum price.

The price of enchantment is contingent on the number of crystal seeds Ilfeen has recharged, and '''not''' on the number of individual equipment pieces she has recharged. For example, a player who pays Ilfeen {{NoCoins|900,000|c}} to enchant a crystal seed into a crystal bow would then only have to pay her {{NoCoins|600,000|c}} to recharge a seed into a crystal shield. Therefore, players who wish to stock up on many pieces of equipment are advised to pay for the shields or halberds first.

==Trivia==
*When [[Song of the Elves]] was released, crystal weapons and crystal seeds were turned into crystal weapon seeds.
*The book, '[[Crystal singing for beginners]]', states that there is no known way to destroy a crystal seed. However, players are able to do so through the [[bank]]'s incinerator feature.
*Once the equipment runs out of charges, the crystal seed remains "equipped" by the player, but it offers no stats and results in [[unarmed]] combat.
*Although crystal seeds are rarely found by players, their exchange price had steadily declined until the release of Song of the Elves, when it could be exchanged for [[crystal acorn]]s via [[Pennant]], as it is very rare for a player to lose a seed without discarding it on purpose. Moreover, it is available from [[Justine's stuff for the Last Shopper Standing]] and, due to being a very popular boss, [[Zulrah]]'s rare crystal seed drop had been encountered many times before its removal from the drop table.

Players can also exchange the weapon seed for 10 [[crystal shard]]s by speaking to [[Amrod]] in [[Prifddinas]]' [[Hefin Inn]]. The seed can additionally be traded to [[Pennant]] in [[Prifddinas]] for one [[crystal acorn]], which can be grown into a crystal tree that yields up to 28-32 crystal shards when harvested.
When converting a crystal seed to a [[crystal bow]] and [[crystal shield]], they '''cannot''' be traded or be used for [[High Level Alchemy|high alchemy]].

===Singing bowl===
After completion of the [[Song of the Elves]] quest players will be able to use crystal shards to sing weapons themselves, requiring 78 [[Crafting]] as well as 78 [[Smithing]]. This can be done at the [[singing bowl]] located just south of the player-owned house portal in the city of [[Prifddinas]]. Another singing bowl can be found in the south-east corner of Prifddinas just east of the mining shop. Players who do not meet the skill requirements can pay a nearby elf to create the weapon for an additional 20 shards.
After completion of [[Song of the Elves]], players may enchant the seeds themselves at a [[Singing bowl]], requiring 78 [[Crafting]] and [[Smithing]].

==Acquiring shards==
As the drop rate for ancient shards are based on the number of [[hitpoints]] a monster has, the best methods of obtaining them will require the player to consider time-to-kill versus drop rate. Attacking multiple monsters at once will give players faster shard rates, making multi-hit attacks such as [[Ice Barrage]], [[black chinchompas]], and the [[venator bow]] the best weapons for this method. Barraging and using chinchompas will be more active, whereas the venator bow allows for a more reclined experience.

Using a [[Dinh's bulwark]] in combination with a [[Lightbearer]] is an efficient way to lure the monsters, as is using a [[Goading potion]]. A cheaper alternative is to use [[Dart|darts]] or [[Knives|knives]].
In addition, when farming shards players can also obtain [[dark totem]] pieces which give access to [[Skotizo]] and by extension more shards due to his guaranteed drops.

Giants in the [[Giants' Den]] have access to the Catacombs of Kourend drop table, which includes dark totem pieces and ancient shards. Killing [[hill giants]] with a [[Dwarf Multicannon]] within it is a comparable method to killing higher level monsters.

Viable monsters to farm shards include [[greater nechryael]]s, [[abyssal demons]], [[Warped Jelly|warped jellies]], and [[dust devils]]. [[Mutated bloodvelds]] can also be viable when using the [[venator bow]], the trade off for lower effort being slower shard acquisition. Being on a slayer task will increase kills per hour, but prioritising that limits the amount of kills players can do consecutively to the length of their task. It is realistic to not get a single shard in the time it takes to complete a slayer task.

At the same time, a message in the [[Chat Interface|chatbox]] will state {{mes|You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.|color=red}} However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a [[cat]]), it will be placed into their [[inventory]]. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state {{mes|You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.|color=red}}

==Colours==
Players can change the Phoenix's colour by using 250 of the desired [[gnomish firelighters]] on it while it is following the player. Doing so unlocks that colour permanently, even if the pet is reclaimed from [[Probita]], and players can switch freely between the unlocked colours.
Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at [[200 million experience|200 million]] [[Firemaking]] experience.

==Trivia==
*Prior to the removal of [[supply crate]]s, it was possible to obtain a phoenix pet while in underwater areas such as the [[Mogre Camp]] and [[Fossil Island]]'s [[underwater]] area.
*Using a [[bucket of water]] on the Phoenix will result in the chatbox stating ''The phoenix dodges the water''. Doing so consumes the bucket of water entirely, including the bucket itself.
* The Phoenix's in-game model is a miniaturisation of the [[Desert Phoenix|Desert Phoenix's]] model.
*The Phoenix's standard dialogue makes several references to pop culture:
**The first and second dialogues are references to Solaire of Astora of ''{{WP|Dark Souls}}''.
**The "long night" mentioned in the first dialogue may be a reference to ''{{WP|A Song of Ice and Fire}}''.
**The Sacred Ash mentioned in the fourth dialogue could be a reference to ''{{WP|Pokémon}}'', where Sacred Ash is an item associated with the Legendary Pokémon Ho-Oh, whose name is derived from a Japanese counterpart to the Western phoenix. It is more likely that it just shares a common characteristic of mythical phoenixes of dying and being reborn from ash.
**Also in the fourth dialogue, the player's confusion about the sky is a reference to RuneScape not having a skybox.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the [[Chat Interface|chatbox]] will state {{mes|You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.|color=red}} However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a [[cat]]), it will be placed into their [[inventory]]. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state {{mes|You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.|color=red}}

==Colours==
Players can change the Phoenix's colour by using 250 of the desired [[gnomish firelighters]] on it while it is following the player. Doing so unlocks that colour permanently, even if the pet is reclaimed from [[Probita]], and players can switch freely between the unlocked colours.
Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at [[200 million experience|200 million]] [[Firemaking]] experience.

==Trivia==
*Prior to the removal of [[supply crate]]s, it was possible to obtain a phoenix pet while in underwater areas such as the [[Mogre Camp]] and [[Fossil Island]]'s [[underwater]] area.
*Using a [[bucket of water]] on the Phoenix will result in the chatbox stating ''The phoenix dodges the water''. Doing so consumes the bucket of water entirely, including the bucket itself.
* The Phoenix's in-game model is a miniaturisation of the [[Desert Phoenix|Desert Phoenix's]] model.
*The Phoenix's standard dialogue makes several references to pop culture:
**The first and second dialogues are references to Solaire of Astora of ''{{WP|Dark Souls}}''.
**The "long night" mentioned in the first dialogue may be a reference to ''{{WP|A Song of Ice and Fire}}''.
**The Sacred Ash mentioned in the fourth dialogue could be a reference to ''{{WP|Pokémon}}'', where Sacred Ash is an item associated with the Legendary Pokémon Ho-Oh, whose name is derived from a Japanese counterpart to the Western phoenix. It is more likely that it just shares a common characteristic of mythical phoenixes of dying and being reborn from ash.
**Also in the fourth dialogue, the player's confusion about the sky is a reference to RuneScape not having a skybox.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the [[Chat Interface|chatbox]] will state {{mes|You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.|color=red}} However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a [[cat]]), it will be placed into their [[inventory]]. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state {{mes|You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.|color=red}}

==Colours==
Players can change the Phoenix's colour by using 250 of the desired [[gnomish firelighters]] on it while it is following the player. Doing so unlocks that colour permanently, even if the pet is reclaimed from [[Probita]], and players can switch freely between the unlocked colours.
Though the Wintertodt is classified as a boss rather than a skilling activity, the phoenix is fifteen times more common at [[200 million experience|200 million]] [[Firemaking]] experience.

==Trivia==
*Prior to the removal of [[supply crate]]s, it was possible to obtain a phoenix pet while in underwater areas such as the [[Mogre Camp]] and [[Fossil Island]]'s [[underwater]] area.
*Using a [[bucket of water]] on the Phoenix will result in the chatbox stating ''The phoenix dodges the water''. Doing so consumes the bucket of water entirely, including the bucket itself.
* The Phoenix's in-game model is a miniaturisation of the [[Desert Phoenix|Desert Phoenix's]] model.
*The Phoenix's standard dialogue makes several references to pop culture:
**The first and second dialogues are references to Solaire of Astora of ''{{WP|Dark Souls}}''.
**The "long night" mentioned in the first dialogue may be a reference to ''{{WP|A Song of Ice and Fire}}''.
**The Sacred Ash mentioned in the fourth dialogue could be a reference to ''{{WP|Pokémon}}'', where Sacred Ash is an item associated with the Legendary Pokémon Ho-Oh, whose name is derived from a Japanese counterpart to the Western phoenix. It is more likely that it just shares a common characteristic of mythical phoenixes of dying and being reborn from ash.
**Also in the fourth dialogue, the player's confusion about the sky is a reference to RuneScape not having a skybox.

cases.semanticExcerpt: '''Mr McGroot''' is a [[pet]] obtained from [[goat hunting|hunting goats]] on [[Wyrmscraig]], a [[Hunter]] training method.
cases.positiveFunctionExcerpt: '''Mr McGroot''' is a [[pet]] obtained from [[goat hunting|hunting goats]] on [[Wyrmscraig]], a [[Hunter]] training method.
secondaryExcerpts: '''Mr McGroot''' is a [[pet]] obtained from [[goat hunting|hunting goats]] on [[Wyrmscraig]], a [[Hunter]] training method.

When a player receives the pet, it will automatically try to appear as their follower. At the same time, a message in the [[Chat Interface|chatbox]] will state {{mes|You have a funny feeling like you're being followed.|color=red}} However, if a player receives a pet while having a follower out (for example, a [[cat]]), it will be placed into their [[inventory]]. When this occurs, the message in the chatbox will instead state {{mes|You feel something weird sneaking into your backpack.|color=red}}
If a player's inventory is full '''and''' they have a follower already, they '''will not''' receive the pet; it must instead be claimed from [[Probita]] in [[East Ardougne]].

==Item sources==
A player's actual chances of receiving it is <math>\frac{1}{B-(Lvl*25)}</math>, where <math display="inline">B</math> is the base chance and <math display="inline">Lvl</math> is the player's Hunter level.
Similar to other pets obtained via skilling, the drop rate increases by 15 times when the player reaches 200 million experience in Hunter, putting the rate at ~1/2501.

==Trivia==
*Mr McGroot's examine text is a reference to {{wp|Groot}}, a character from {{wp|Marvel Comics}}.
*Mr McGroot is the only pet that does not appear in any [[collection log]] pages other than the 'All Pets' page.
